this is yet another layer of the secrets of body and speech.
Chan Master Guizong Chang succeeded the Dharma of Master Daemao of Silla.
One day, as he ascended the hall, he said: "If you wish to recognize the Teacher of all Buddhas, seek him within the mind of ignorance. If you wish to recognize...
The nature of eternal non-decay is to be recognized within the realm of the shifting and changing of all things. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dameao?
The Master said, "Not revealing the edge. The monk asked, "Why do you not reveal the edge? The Master said, "Because there is no one who can meet it."

Baotán said: It does not mean that within the mind of ignorance there exists separately some teacher of the Buddhas, nor that within the shifting transformations of the myriad trees there exists separately a permanent, non-decaying nature. Rather, once the mind of ignorance is shattered, the teachers of the Buddhas are spontaneously present therein;
and when one clearly perceives the shifting transformations of the myriad trees, the permanent, non-decaying nature is likewise found.
To speak in such a manner is called "healing a dead horse.
Zen Master Zhìtōng of Wǔtái called himself a "Great Chan Buddha. Initially, while he was under the guidance at Guīzōng, one night he suddenly cried out repeatedly, saying, "I am the Great..."

He attained awakening. The assembly was astonished by this. The next day, when Guizong ascended the hall and the assembly had just gathered, Guizong said, "The monk who had a great awakening last night—come forward.
The Master stepped forward and said, "I am he. Guizong asked, "What principle have you seen that you speak of a 'great awakening'?
Try to explain it. The Master said, "A nun is originally made of womanhood. Guizong marveled at this, and the Master then took his leave.
The head monk escorted him out and handed him his straw hat. The Master took the hat, placed it on his head, and walked away without looking back.
Later, he resided at Fahua Temple on Mount Tai. At the time of his death, he said: "Raising my hand, I grasp the Southern Dipper; turning my body, I lean against the Northern Pole.
Looking out from beyond the heavens, who is there like me?"
Baotán said: "Zhìtōng captured the thief at midnight, yet no one could bring the matter to a final conclusion.

It was only when Guīzōng examined and verified the case at dawn that the thief was apprehended along with the stolen goods. This is what is meant by 'the blue felt on the rack is an old possession of my own house';
why else would it have fallen into the hands of a thief? Thus we know that today's thieves were the sages of former days. Why do I say this?"
He raised his hand to grasp the Southern Dipper and turned his body to lean against the Northern Pole. How could this be within the reach of the common world?
Among students, there are those who recognize the thief but cannot capture him, and those who can capture the thief yet it is not the real thief.
Only one like Zhizhong, who experienced a moment of profound exhilaration, may truly be said to have fulfilled his life's purpose.
Formerly, Chan Master Lingyou of Mount Gui succeeded the Dharma of Chan Master Huiji of Yangshan in Yuanzhou.
When the Master first visited Mount Gui, he ascended to the inner sanctum. Lingyou asked him, "Are you a novice with a master, or one without a master?"
The śrāmaṇera said, "It has a master. Dàoyòu asked, "Where is it? The Master walked from west to east and stood there. Dàoyòu held him in high regard. He then gave this instruction:

The Master asked, "What is the dwelling place of the True Buddha? Dàoyòu replied, "By means of the wondrous state of thinking without thinking, one returns to the thought that the spiritual flame is inexhaustible.
When thinking is exhausted, one returns to the source; nature and form are eternally present, and phenomena and principle are non-dual."

The Buddha is simply suchness (*tathatā*). Under these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. Later, he visited Yantou. Yantou raised his whisk; the Master spread out his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*).
Yantou took up the whisk and placed it behind his back; the Master draped the sitting cloth over his shoulder and departed.
Tou said, "I do not consent to your letting go; I only consent to your gathering it in. He then visited Shishi (Shishim), asking, "How far apart are the Buddha and the Way?
Shishi replied, "The Way is like an outstretched hand; the Buddha is like a clenched fist. Thereupon, he took his leave of Shishi.
As the master saw him off at the gate, he called out, "My son, do not go away forever; come back to my side later. Wei Zhou requested a verse from Muzhou (Weishan).
Shan said, "To present face-to-face is still the mark of a dull-witted person; how much more so when it is expressed through paper and brush? He then requested instruction from the Master.
The Master drew a circle on a piece of paper and annotated it, saying: "To know it through thought falls into the second head;
to know it without thought falls into the third head. One day, while accompanying Guishan as he was clearing a field, he asked, "Why is this end so low?"
"That peak is so high," [the Master] said. Huìyù replied, "Water can level things; simply use water to level it. The Master said, "Water is unreliable.
You, Master, should simply level what is high by making it high, and level what is low by making it low. Huìyù approved of this.
When a donor arrived with silk, the Master asked, "The Master accepts such offerings from donors; how do you repay them? Huìyù struck [the ground].
He pointed to his meditation seat. The Master said, "How can you take the property of the assembly and use it as your own? Dàoyù suddenly asked the Master, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I have come from the fields. Dàoyù asked, "How many people are in the fields? The Master stood there with his spade thrust into the ground.
Dàoyù said, "Today on South Mountain, there are many people cutting thatch. The Master raised his spade and departed. [Later], the Master was herding oxen.
At that time, the Head Seat asked, "A hundred billion maned lions appear. The Master did not answer; he returned to his station and stood in attendance.
When the Head Seat came forward to inquire after him, the Master raised the previous remark and asked, "Just now you said, 'A hundred billion maned lions appear.
Did you not say this, Head Seat? He replied, "I did. The Master said, "At the very moment they appear, do they appear before the fur, or do they appear behind the fur? The Head Seat said, "..."
At that moment, he did not speak of before or after, and the Master stepped forward. Huìyǒu said, "The lion’s waist has broken.
While the Master and Guishan were walking, a crow dropped a red persimmon in front of them. Guishan was about to give it to the Master;
the Master took it, washed it, and then gave it back to Guishan. Guishan asked, "Where did you get this? The Master replied, "This is what the Master said."
Moved by his virtue, Guishan said, "You must not leave empty-handed," and he immediately divided half [of his seat] and gave it to him.

Later, when the Master resided at Yangshan, he ascended the hall and said: "All of you, turn your light inward and look back; do not merely memorize my words. Since beginningless kalpas, you have turned your backs on the light and cast yourselves into darkness;
the roots of your deluded thoughts are deep and firm, making them difficult to uproot suddenly. Therefore, I provisionally establish these methods."
To then seize your coarse consciousness is like using yellow leaves to stop a child’s crying; what propriety is there in this?
It is also like a person who takes a hundred kinds of goods and sells them as a single shop of gold and jewels, intending only to test the discernment of their weight.
Therefore it is said: "Shitou’s place is a shop of pure gold; my place here is a general store.
If someone comes seeking mouse droppings, I likewise pick them up and give them to him; if they come seeking pure gold, I likewise pick it up and give it to them. At that time, a monk asked:
"Mouse droppings are simply not wanted; I request the Venerable Master’s true gold. The Master said, "To gnaw at the arrowhead is like intending to open one's mouth;
even in a donkey-year, you will not understand. The monk had no reply. The Master said, "If you call out for it, there is a transaction; if you do not call out for it, there is none.
If I were to speak of the Chan school, I would not have a single person to accompany me by my side, let alone a congregation of five hundred or seven hundred."
Yes. If I were to speak of east as west, you would scramble forward with your heads to pick it up; it would be like deceiving a small child with an empty fist—there is no substance to it at all.
I shall now clearly explain to you the matters concerning the side of the Sage. For now, do not let your mind settle upon them;
simply practice according to reality within the ocean of your own nature. You need not seek the three knowledges or six supernormal powers. Why is this?
This is merely a matter of peripheral details. For now, you must simply recognize the mind and penetrate the source. If you attain the source, you need not worry about the periphery;
at some future time, it will naturally be complete. If you have not attained the source, even if you apply your emotions and study others, you will not achieve it.
Have you not heard the Venerable Master of Mt. Wei say: "When the sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted, the true permanence of the essence is revealed"?

The non-duality of phenomena and principle is the Buddha of Suchness (Tathatā). Consequently, he went to Mount Gui to pay his respects to Baizhang Huaiyu. Huaiyu asked him, "You call yourself a 'Good Knowledge-Holder' (Kalyāṇamitra).
How do you distinguish between those who come from all quarters—whether they know it or do not know it, whether they have a teacher or no teacher?"
"This is the study of meaning; this is metaphysics. You, my son, try to explain it. The Master said, "Huiji has a point of verification.
Whenever I see monks coming from various quarters, I simply raise my whisk and ask them: 'Do you people from all quarters speak of this, or not? He further said:

"Let this matter rest for now. What is the intention of the venerable elders of all quarters? Huizhao sighed and said, "This one is a true talon and fang from among the ancestral patriarchs of the Gate of the School.
Huizhao asked, "The karmic consciousness of all sentient beings in the great earth is vast and boundless, with no fundamental basis to rely upon.
How do you know whether it exists or not? The Master replied, "Huiji has a way to verify it. At that time, there was a monk present.
As the monk passed by in front of him, the Master called out, "Acarya! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "Elder. The monk replied, "Venerable Master.
The Master remarked, "This is precisely what is called 'the karmic consciousness wandering aimlessly, with no fundamental basis to rely upon.

Yunju said, "This is but a single drop of lion’s milk that scatters six bushels of donkey’s milk. A monk asked, "Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma? The Master said, "I do not speak."
[The Master] said, "I have attained it. Another person said, "I have attained it. The Abbot asked, "Where is the person who says they have attained it?
The Master pushed out his meditation pillow. When Guishan heard of this, he said, "Jizi (the Silent Son) uses the sword's edge.
One day, as the Master was passing before Guishan’s Dharma Hall, Guishan saw him and said, "If you are truly a son of our late master Baizhang, you must receive a severe beating before you will do."
Baotán said: "The 'Penetration of the Essence' (zōngtōng) and the 'Penetration of the Teaching' (shuōtōng) are matters pertaining to the station of true Buddhas and patriarchs.

Having already reached this point through the intimate guidance of the father and son of Míngyáng—who personally took one another by the arm—what greater glory could there be in wishing to further lead and support them from the left and right, transcending even the Buddhas and patriarchs?
Nevertheless, one must also discuss whether their innate disposition is robust, firm, and pure. Since ancient times...
Refinement can preserve a family; rigidity can destroy a family—this is the inevitability of principle.
Deshan and Linji were sons who destroyed their families; Muzhou and Yangshan, father and son, were truly sons who preserved their families.
Yet, preservation inevitably leads to a gradual decline into insignificance, whereas destruction allows for the subsequent establishment of something new—this is the inevitability of circumstance.
One day, Yangshan was passing in front of the Dharma Hall at Mount Muzhou when Muzhou said, "If you were truly a son of our late master Baizhang, you would have to endure a severe beating.
This was indeed so; when Mazu, Deshan, Linji, and their respective disciples engaged one another in exhaustive interrogation, they would invariably return to the fundamental source.
Examining his life's work, Yangshan’s galloping spirit transcended all traces, like a horse in a field.
Inserting the spade and pushing out the pillow—these are all matters concerning the edge of the sword. All others do not emerge from within the stage of faith or the stage of the person.
Jiji occupies the position of the master and returns to visit his teacher; father and son engage in debate.

This is the exemplary conduct of a *kalyāṇamitra* for the sake of others, possessing the claws and fangs of the ancestral school of the Gateless Barrier and the essential principle of "a single drop of lion’s milk."
This is also a discourse that remains unshakable for ten thousand generations. A father’s love for his son persists from infancy until adulthood;

his heart of deep affection never forgets him for even a moment. When the son reaches this stage, he can be entrusted with the protection of the family, and though the father closes his eyes in death, he has no regrets.
I am moved by these sentiments, and thus I have expressed them through the example of the masters of the Wei and Yang lineages, father and son.
When Chan Master Xiangyan Zhixian of Dengzhou first visited Chan Master Daoyou of Mount Gui, the Master wished to bring forth his intellectual radiance and said to him:
"I shall not ask you about your lifelong studies and understandings, nor what you have memorized from books. Before you had emerged from the womb, before you could distinguish east from west—"
"Regarding the fundamental matter at hand, try to offer a single phrase; I wish to take note of you. The Master was bewildered and had no reply.
After reflecting for a long time, he offered several words to express his understanding, but Yunju rejected them all. The Master said, "I beg the Master to explain it for me.
Yunju said, "What I can explain is only my own understanding; what benefit would that be for your own eyes? Thereupon, the Master...

Returning to his quarters, he searched through all the collections he had gathered, but not a single sentence could serve as a match for what he sought. He sighed to himself, saying, "A painted cake cannot satisfy hunger.

Thereupon, he burned them all, declaring, "In this life, I shall not study the Buddha-dharma. I will instead become a simple monk who travels from place to place to receive alms, so as to spare my mind and spirit from such toil.
He then wept as he took leave of Master Muzhou and traveled to Nanyang, where he arrived at the remains of National Teacher Huizhong.
He rested there. One day, while clearing away grass and trees in the mountains, he struck a bamboo with a piece of tile and produced a sound.
Suddenly, amidst a burst of laughter, he attained a vast self-awakening and immediately returned home. He bathed, burned incense, and paid remote homage to Mount Miao, offering this praise:
"The Great Compassion of the Master is a kindness exceeding that of my own parents. Had you explained it to me at that time, how could there have been the circumstances of today? Thus it was.
He spoke in verse: "A single blow causes all that is known to be forgotten; Thereafter, no further cultivation or refinement is required.

In every place, there are no traces; Beyond sound and form lies true dignified demeanor. Those who have realized the Way in all directions All say this is the highest capacity. Later, while residing at Xiangyan, he ascended the hall and said:

The Way is attained through awakening; it does not reside in words and phrases. Moreover, seeing that which is dense and majestic, there has never been any separation. There is no need for mental effort;

simply turn the light back for a moment, and the full function is present in daily life. Deluded followers merely turn their backs on this themselves. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Xiangyan? The Master said:
"Flowers and trees do not flourish. Question: "What is *siddhārtha* (仙陀婆)? The Master struck the meditation seat and said: [Siddhārtha].
[The Master] called him over. He asked, "What is present study? The Master rotated his fan and showed it to him, saying, "Do you see it?
The monk was speechless. He asked, "What is food obtained through right livelihood? The Master pinched him with his hand and showed it to him.
He asked, "What is unmanifest precept (avijñapti-śīla)? The Master said, "I will explain it once you have become a layman. He asked, "What are sounds and forms?"
Regarding the phrase "seeing external forms," the Master said, "Before I resided at Xiangyan, where did you say the Way was?
The monk said, "At such a time, I would not dare say it is located anywhere. The Master said, "It is like the mind and its mental objects of an illusory person."
A monk asked, "When one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spiritual nature, what then?

The Master said, "The myriad functions are brought to rest; even the thousand sages cannot carry them away. Shushan, who was among the assembly, made a sound of retching and said, "What kind of talk is this?

The Master asked, "Who is that? The assembly replied, "It is the Master’s junior uncle (Shushan). The Master said, "Why did he not acknowledge me, old monk? Shushan came forward and said, "Yes. The Master said, "Do not say that!"
[The monk] said, "I have attained it. The Master said, "Speak it! [The monk] said, "If you command me to speak, I must first return the courtesy of teacher and disciple.

The Master then descended from his seat and prostrated. Stepping forward, he asked the previous question. Shushan said, "Why do you not say, 'Though one may acknowledge the weight, one cannot possess it in its entirety'?
The Master said, "Even if you were as capable as that, you would still have to vomit for thirty years. Even if you were to dwell on a mountain, there would be no [benefit]."
"If you burn firewood near water, you will have no water to drink. Take this clearly to heart. Later, while residing at Shushan, it turned out exactly as his teacher had predicted.
In the twenty-seventh year, his illness was cured; he said of himself, "My senior brother Xiangyan predicted that I would vomit for thirty years. Now I am three years short.
Every time I finish eating, I use my hand to pick out the food and spit it out, in order to fulfill that previous prediction. A monk asked, "How about..."
This was the first phrase of the sound. The Master said, "Virtuous One, I have already answered before you even asked.
The monk asked, "What does 'immediately' mean? The Master said, "It is the very moment of asking. The monk asked, "What is the direct source of the root, sealed by the Buddhas?
The Master threw down his staff and walked away with his hands open. [Another] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The frost descends this year."
"Early! No wheat at all. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master reached his hand into his robe, drew out his fist, opened it wide, and presented it to him.
The monk then knelt and made a gesture with both hands as if receiving something. The Master said, "What is this? The monk was speechless.
A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "A dragon’s roar from a withered tree. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A skull..."

The eyeballs within the skull. One day he said to the assembly: "Suppose a person is at the edge of a thousand-fathom precipice, with a tree branch in his mouth, his feet having no place to tread and his hands nothing to grasp. Suddenly someone asks, 'What is the meaning of the West?
If he opens his mouth to answer, he will lose his body and forfeit his life; if he does not answer, he violates the questioner's inquiry. At such a moment, what would you do?"
"How is it? At that time, the Venerable Zhao stepped forward and said, "I do not ask about when he has already climbed the tree;
how was it before he had climbed the tree? The Master simply smiled.
Baotan said: "If one does not first eliminate the outflows of desire, then the accumulation of learning will become a fault.
[The verse] 'Mistakenly taking the one who upholds the Buddha's teachings as the Buddha'—why would the Buddha not himself hear what is heard? This was spoken by the Great Being Mañjuśrī to Ānanda.
Although Xian’s extensive learning did not equal that of Ānanda, his failure to hear the Way was roughly the same in magnitude. At the time Xian was at Bai Zhang, [he was still a student].

In the prime of his youth, he could answer ten questions for every one asked, and a hundred for every ten; though his brilliance was like a torch and his calculations were as precise as those of others, all were but the treasures of another.
One day, however, the winds of karma blew him up to Mount Miao, where his worldly livelihood was swept away and left utterly empty.
He then resolutely descended to Lake Dongting and traveled through Xianghan, eventually settling on an ancient site in Nanyang to dwell among the mountains.
Clouds drifted back and forth and wild birds chattered; there was no longer anything from former times to disturb the mind.

From then on, eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, he relied entirely upon its power. One day, as he struck a bamboo stalk and it produced a sharp, resonant sound, the message that existed prior to the birth of his parents was revealed.
Thereupon, he prostrated himself before Muzhou and composed this verse: "A single strike causes me to forget all else."

"Understood. Thereafter, the discourse on no longer requiring further cultivation was established, and from that time forth, the Chan of the Tathāgata and the Chan of the Patriarchs were disseminated throughout all quarters.
The Chan of the Tathāgata concerns matters within the threshold; the Chan of the Patriarchs concerns matters beyond the threshold.
Thus it is said: "Within the threshold, the Son of Heaven exercises control; beyond the threshold, the General exercises control. To climb a tree at the end of one's life—this is the meaning.
This is not something that can be confined by either the Tathāgata-dhyāna or the Patriarchal-dhyāna.

When Chan Master Hongyin of Mount Jing in Hangzhou first visited Yunyan, their karmic conditions did not harmonize; he then went to Moshan, where his lingering doubts were suddenly dispelled. Following the Huichang persecution...
He returned [to his home province]. In the sixth year of the Xiántóng era, he became the third patriarch of Jìngshān.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the breath is stilled like ashes? The Master said, "It is still the effort of worldly people. The monk asked, "What is it like after that effort?

The Master said, "The plowman tills the field but does not sow. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it like? The Master said, "When the grain is ripe, one does not go to the market. A monk asked, "The Dragon Gate..."
"If one can penetrate it without relying on the power of wind and thunder, how is that? The Master said, "That is still only the first or second grade.
The monk asked, "Since this consists of such stages, what is the matter beyond them? The Master said, "I do not know whether you have the Dragon Gate."
A monk asked, "What is it like when it is like frost and like snow? The Master said, "It is still a defilement.

The monk asked, "What is it like when there is no defilement? The Master said, "Not entirely colored. The Venerable Quanming of Xuzhou once asked Shishuang, "When a single hair pierces through all the holes, what then?
Shishuang said, "One must wait until ten thousand years later. The monk asked, "What is it like after ten thousand years? Shishuang—
Shuangyun said, "As for passing the examinations, let you pass them; as for excelling among the elite, let you excel.

Later, he asked the Master, "What is it like when a single hair pierces through many holes? The Master said, "As for polishing your boots, let you polish them; as for reaching the final result, let you reach it."
A monk asked, "What is long? The Master said, "Even the thousand sages cannot measure it. The monk asked, "What is short?
The Master said, "It would not even fill the eye of a tiny gnat. The monk did not approve and departed.

He recounted this to Shishuang, who said, "It was only because you were too close to the literal reality. The monk asked, "What is long? Shishuang said, "Without bending. [The monk] asked, "What is..."

[The Master] said, "Short. Frosted clouds. In the game of *shuangliu* (double-six), one does not cry out for cheers. The Elder Furi visited the Master and asked, "I have heard that you, Elder, have been uniquely transforming this region.
Why do you travel so frequently to the mountain peaks? Furi replied, "A bright moon hangs suspended in the sky."
"Frost does not freeze itself. The Master said, "Is this not the family style of the Elder? Furi said, "A myriad steep passes stand tall; within them lies the precious moon.
The Master said, "This is still merely literary expression. What is the family style of the Elder? He replied, "Today I am fortunate to have met Furi.
Furi then asked, "When one is completely true to the hidden and secret, what do people of the present day [do]?"

To know that there is a Way yet not attain it; to greatly realize one’s innocence when people know there is a Way and attain it—these two paths are still the points where ordinary people ascend or descend.
I do not yet know how you, Elder, personally embody the Way and speak of the Way yourself. The Master said: "In my house, where the Way resides, there is no 'Way' at all.
Furong Daokai said: "On the Path of the Tathāgata, there is no partiality or crookedness. Please, let us hear your profound voice."
One round was harmonized. The Master said: "Let the two orbs shine upon each other as they will; the azure pool beyond the clouds remains unrelated. Furi said:
"To inform the infinite multitude of white-haired elders: this time, young men, do not return to your hometowns. The Master said:
"Old and young share the same wheel, without front or back; let there be no discrepancy on the profound path of my house. Furi said: "A single word settles the empire."
The Master said, "For whom are the four lines reserved? You say there are three or four; I say that not even one among them exists.
Later, he found his son at Milei and showed him [the verse], saying, "Nothing surpasses this. A monk asked, "I do not yet understand what it is that nothing surpasses.
Milei said, "It does not go beyond this. Later, that monk asked Changqing, "Why does it not go beyond?"
"Exactly. Changqing said, "What do you intend to call it?
Baotan said, "The pivot-wheel is that which turns of itself without being pushed. The ancients took empty space and the great earth as their pivot-wheels, operating with sovereign freedom;
they took the golden circle and the thorn-berry as their pivot-wheels, playing freely within them."
Therefore, the pivot is the instrument that carries the student to the great ocean of the Buddha-dharma;
it is the instrument that pushes the wheel of the deluded stream out of the path of birth and death. Thus, the pivot must not be absent for even a single day. Someone may ask:
"In the case of those such as Zhizhe (Zhigong) who struck the ground, what further use would there be for a pivot? This person likely does not understand the two elders.
The pivot of this mechanism is like the swords Ganjiang and Moye; its edge cannot be withstood, and those who encounter it will surely die—it is this very mechanism.
Master Yìn turned the upper bolt and struck the primordial pivot; it was like a whirlwind or a wheel of fire.
One does not know how many people perished at his hands at that time, yet only his son, Miling, [survived].
Once the Master’s single phrase appeared in writing, it was difficult for Wenyi’s hand to handle it.
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin of Fuzhou, when he was first at Mount Guiyang, attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms and said: "For thirty years I have sought a swordsman."
How many times have fallen leaves sprouted branches again? Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, until now, I have never again harbored any doubt.
When Guishan read this verse, he questioned the monk about its origins; it was found to be in perfect accord with his own realization.

Guishan said, "To awaken through conditions and reach full understanding means you shall never again fall back or lose what you have attained. Guard and maintain it well. Later, a monk brought this up to Xuansha, who said, "It is most precise and correct."
"It is true. I dare say that you, elder brother, have not yet attained thorough penetration. The assembly doubted these words and asked Xuansha to question Dizang:
"When he speaks thus, how do you understand it? Dizang said, "If it were not Guichen, he would have run the whole world to death.
The Master returned to Minchuan and addressed the assembly, saying: "O worthy ones, all things—whether long or short—are ultimately impermanent. Now, observe the four..."

At that time, the leaves of the grasses and trees fall and the flowers bloom; how much more so for the heavens, humans, and the seven realms of existence throughout kalpas as numerous as motes of dust, through the cycles of formation and destruction by earth, water, fire, and wind?
When the fruits of karma are exhausted, the sufferings of the three evil paths do not increase or decrease by even a hair’s breadth.

Only the root, which carries the divine consciousness, remains eternally present. Those of superior capacity who encounter virtuous friends clarify their state and attain liberation in that very place; this is the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).

Those of middling and inferior capacity, being dull-witted and ignorant, are unable to awaken or attain clear illumination. They remain mired in the three realms, wandering through the cycle of birth and death.
For their sake, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni established teachings in both the heavens and among humans, manifesting and clarifying the Path of Wisdom. Do you all understand?
At that time, a monk asked, "How can one escape from birth, old age, sickness, and death? The Master said, "The green mountains have never moved; floating clouds drift by."
Qilai asked, "What is it like when the sovereign goes forth into battle? The Master said, "Outside the Chunming Gate, one does not ask about Chang'an.
The monk asked, "How does one have an audience with the Son of Heaven? The Master said, "A blind crane descends into the clear pond; a fish passes beneath its feet."

Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "The donkey’s business is not yet over; the horse’s business has arrived. Question: "I have not yet grasped the profound principle;
I pray you will grant me further instruction. The Master said: "The auspicious vapor moves constantly at night; the spiritual essence is rarely encountered by day. Changsheng asked:
"Before the primordial chaos was divided, from where did sentient beings come? The Master said: "It is like a pillar conceiving a child. [Changsheng] said: "Once it was divided..."

The person who recorded this was the Abbot of the Hall of Human and Heavenly Eyes. Having realized the Master’s intent, he subsequently laid down his staff;
he then summoned the First Seat to open the hall and preach the Dharma as the abbot.

Baotan said: "I have no leisure to exhaustively investigate the spiritual efficacy of Lingshu. I shall merely observe the saying that 'the field of a thousand years has eight hundred owners' and the words regarding the wind-wheel atop the Fire Official's head;
these are sufficient to recognize Yunmen even before his birth, let alone after he was born. The eye of a true friend and the Buddha-eye have places where they do not reach."
Aniruddha said, “I view the trichiliocosm as if looking at an *āmra* fruit in the palm of my hand;
it is almost like a small vessel that is easily filled. Vimalakīrti said, “There is a Buddha, a World-Honored One, who possesses the true divine eye;
he is just right for eating the staff of the *lingshu* tree. Do you wish to know whether the eye of the *lingshu* tree is blind?”
The Great Master Huiri of Guohuan in Quanzhou was, in his youth, a prison guard in Hougan County of Fuzhou.

He frequently abandoned his duties and went to the presence of the Venerable Shenguang Lingguan and later to the Venerable Dajian of Xiyuan; the officials were unable to restrain him. Afterwards, he visited Wansui Tankong.
The Chan Master shaved his head, yet he did not don the *kāṣāya* nor receive full ordination; he wore only a sash made of five-colored silk.
He then went to the place of Master Guan, who said, "I am not your teacher. Go and pay your respects at Xiyuan.
Carrying a small green bamboo staff, the Master entered the Dharma Hall of Xiyuan. Seeing him from afar, Master An smiled and said, "Enter the Nirvana Hall."
"Go. The Master assented and entered with his bamboo staff in hand. At that time, there were about five hundred monks suffering from an epidemic.

The Master tapped them one by one with his staff, and each rose as soon as he was tapped. The King of Min paid him reverent homage and established a monastery for him within the state to serve as his residence.
Baotan said: "This is Huang Niepan (Yellow Nirvana). Because he entered the Nirvana Hall of Xiyuan, he was called 'Nirvana.
He dwelt permanently at Bichizhi Rock, and was thus also called 'Bichizhi. Upon seeing Lingguan and Da'an, he passed away. This Master discoursed on emptiness;
he used five-colored cloth for his robes and a green bamboo staff as his cane—what need was there for any other karmic conditions? Xuefeng led his disciples southward..."
As [Zhao] Youpan was traveling, Feng anticipated his arrival and met him with staff in hand at Gusu. Feng asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
Youpan replied, "Pizhi Rock. Feng said, "Is there anyone residing at that rock? Youpan struck Feng’s sedan chair with his bamboo staff.
Fengchou came out to meet him. Xuedou Pan said, "Wanfú to the Master. Fengchou hastily performed a man’s bow, while Pan performed a woman’s bow.
Fengchou asked, "Are you not a woman? Pan bowed twice more, then used his bamboo staff to scratch the ground, circling Fengchou’s sedan chair three times.
Xuefeng recognized his realization and immediately invited him to enter the mountains; Pan then prepared various extraordinary provisions.

Ah! I do not know whether he was a sage or an ordinary man. I only know that when he met Xuefeng, he employed the "nose-tip" of a monk (*nam-seng ba-bei*), which cannot be constrained by anything within or without the three realms. Is he perhaps a peer of the two disciples Han and Shi?
Otherwise, one who muddles the holy and sinks into the mundane would find it difficult to cast off his shoes; such a person is not what we call a monk.
While they were deliberating on this matter,
Master Fojian of Mount Fujiang arrived,
leading a group of disciples from Xuefeng. He asked, "At present, there are two hundred people staying at the monastery."
Xia De also said, "There is none. The Master took up his staff, drew a line on the ground, and said, "If you cannot grasp it, then speak!
Xuefeng was speechless.
This was the Venerable Lushui of Luzhou.

A monk asked the Master, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Have you ever seen the flower and medicinal plant railing in the courtyard? The monk was speechless.

Baotán said: "A thousand explanations and ten thousand expositions are not equal to seeing him face-to-face once. Even one who has seen through the bottom of things is ultimately different [from the master].
Xuefeng’s two hundred followers had a vast and imposing air, yet they were not enough to withstand a single stroke across the Yangtze River; at that moment, they surrendered."
"Clear waters and flowering medicinal balustrades—why so many? People of the present day merely waste their efforts on elaborate rhetoric;
in the end, they do not reach the ground of the ancients. Where does the sickness lie?
Formerly, Chan Master Congshen of Zhaozhou succeeded the Dharma of Venerable Yanyang of Xinxing in Hongzhou.
Once, when a monk asked him, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "A clod of earth. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The ground."
[The Master] moved. A monk asked, "What is a monk? The Master said, "Eating porridge, eating rice.
A monk asked, "What is the water of Xingxing? The Master said, "In the river before you. A monk asked, "How does one manifest form in response to things?
The Master said, "Bring me the bench over here. The Master was constantly accompanied on his left and right by a snake and a tiger, whom he fed from his own hand.
[He] ate.
Baotan said: "You bear a striking resemblance to your father. Yan Yang resembles Zhaozhou.
Yan’s recorded encounters consist of no more than these few words, yet they are majestic, profound, and towering, possessing the very skeletal structure of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Like...
Since there is neither Buddha nor Patriarch within his breast, why was he placed among the records of Zhaozhou? How can one distinguish him?
Generally speaking, those who possess what is called the "hand of killing and enlivening" must employ the Vajra King’s Precious Sword and the Iron Stake of Yanyang.
Those struck by the sword would surely die; as for those not struck, how far removed are they from mere rubble?
Rare! Zen Master Huijiao of Guangxiao Monastery in Yangzhou was once asked by a monk:
"When the flowers of awakening first bloom, they fill all of Sahā; now that the Patriarch has come from the West, what matter does he intend to discuss?"
The Master said, "When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed. The monk said, "This is the meaning of the teachings. The Master asked, "What clothes are you wearing?
The monk asked, "What is it like when a single blow shatters empty space? The Master said, "If you are weary, then rest. The Master asked Song Qiqiu, "Do you understand?
Song said, "Even the Way cannot be applied here. The Master said, "There is that which cannot be applied; there is also that which can be applied."
“Not so,” said Song. “It is not like that at all,” the Master replied. Song said, “What about that which cannot be grasped? Song was speechless. The Master led the assembly out;
seeing a pillar, he joined his palms and said, “How do you do, World-Honored One? A monk said, “The Master is the pillar. The Master said, “Crying until the blood flows is of no use;
it is better to keep one’s mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. The monk said, “Far away...”
Yuantou asked the Master, "What is your intention? The Master said, "The authorities are strict; they do not permit any arrangements. Yuan said, "Is there no expedient means?
The Master said, "For now, you may stay one night in the fire-storage room. Layman Zhang asked, "What about old age? The Master said, "How old are you? Zhang said, "Eighty.
The Master said, "One can truly be called 'old'. Zhang asked, "In the final analysis, what is it?"

The Master said, "Even after a thousand years, it still has not been settled. Someone asked, "If someone were to ask me whether there is sin in killing an ox throughout one's life, what would you say?
The Master said, "There is no sin. The man asked, "Why is there no sin? The Master said, "For every one killed, one is returned."
Baotán said: "This is the 'Iron Beak of Awareness. Its application is like lightning, followed immediately by a thunderclap;
its ability to stir dragons and snakes and disperse clouds and rain is exemplified in his meeting with Fǎyǎn. As for striking the water-dragon and shattering the pillar—"
This causes people to sigh that they are like those who cover their ears too late. This is evidenced by the dialogues between Song Qichu and the assembly of monks.
When Yuanjue arrived at Fayen’s place, there was the remark, "Do not slander the former master.
I, the fool, say that Fayen let Ironbeak off the hook, which resulted in his slandering Zhaozhou; Ironbeak did not recognize Zhaozhou, which resulted in his deceiving him.
The Dharma Eye. Those who study today must seek to see the ancients; take care not to slander them yourself.

At Guoqing Monastery in Longzhou, Master Chan Master Feng was asked by a monk, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The rain nourishes the three types of grass, making them flourish in spring."
The wind does not wrap one’s head. A monk asked, "Ultimately, is this one or two? The Master said, "Auspicious clouds rise in competition;
the mountain caves remain unimpaired. He asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "The table, the chair, the brazier, and the window."
Question: "What is it to be an ordained monk? The Master said: "Copper head, iron forehead; bird beak, deer body. Question:
"What is the fundamental matter of an ordained monk? The Master said: "Good morning, [I hope you are] well; good night, take care. A monk asked:
"When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did birds and beasts bring him flowers? The Master said: "It is like a person from Shanfu sending [a gift]."
"Money and an Iron Ox. A monk asked, "After seeing [the ox], why does it not carry flowers? The Master said, "A wooden horse travels eight hundred miles at dawn.
A monk asked, "How does one subdue the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "Striking ice to seek fire; one would not encounter it even after eons.

A monk asked, "The twelve divisions of the teachings are for the purpose of silencing a child's crying. Setting aside this 'silencing the crying,' I ask [for instruction]. The Master said, "A wooden horse travels eight hundred miles at dawn."
The Master’s single phrase: The Master said, “A two-horned woman atop a solitary peak. Question: “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said: “Śākyamuni is the Ox-Head Hell-Warden; the Patriarch is the Horse-Faced Ābāng. Question: “What is the meaning of the [Master’s] coming from the West?
The Master said: “Striking the west wall with the east wall. Question: “What is the phrase that cannot be shattered? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
It is said: "There is not even a hair’s breadth of separation.
People of the time looked up to this in awe. Baotan remarked: "Guoqing’s response to the question posed by the Fourth Patriarch at Niutou is the most outstanding of all.
While there have been many who have faced this question throughout ancient and modern times, they generally answered for themselves; it likely did not pertain to the era of Niutou’s Lanyong."
Only Nanquan alone was one who truly attained it; I have already spoken of this in general terms in my commentary on the biography of Layman Rong.
Now, having come to cherish Guoqing’s words, I shall further elucidate them: "The ancients had straight noses and slanted eyes."
There is no exaggeration, depreciation, praise, or blame within these words. Qingzhi’s extraordinary brilliance does not fall short of Jue Tiezi, and his witty remarks reach far and wide.
His responses to the "Great Meaning of the Buddha Dharma" and the "Meaning of Coming from the West" are both capable of reviving the true lineage of Master Mazu;
through them, future generations will enter the stream of the teaching and certainly avoid living in vain or dying in obscurity.

The student did not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, all bent. A monk asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
The Master said, "There are many who harbor doubts about this. The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Hiding one's head within the moon."
Baotán said: "One stem, two stems—slanting; three stems, four stems—curving. Nowadays, people understand this merely as a response to a question.
Have they not heard how the late Master Huìtáng entered through this very path? Later, while passing a village temple at night, he heard a boy reciting the *Universal Gate Chapter* (*Pumenpin*).
When it reached the passage: "If there are those who should be saved by means of this body, he immediately manifests this body," [the Master attained realization].

He then preached the Dharma for him, whereupon he attained great enlightenment and realized that the Patriarch’s principle of "directly pointing at the human mind to see one's nature and become a Buddha" is by no means a matter of words or written characters.
Even the movement of the wind, the rising of dust, the crowing of a cock, or the barking of a dog—all these are points from which my own awakening is triggered. Let students recognize this.
While Master Xi Mu of Yizhou was presiding over the assembly in the Dharma hall, a layman raised his hand and said, "Master, you are nothing but a donkey. The Master replied:
"The old monk has been mounted by you. The other remained silent. Three days after he had left, he returned and said, "I was robbed by bandits three days ago.
The Master picked up his staff and drove him out. At times, the Master would suddenly call out, "Attendant! and the attendant would respond, "Yes?"
The Master said, "When the night is deep and quiet, we shall deliberate with him together.
Baotan remarked, "In another time, this was also the case throughout the whole of Shu; the common folk knew for themselves that three days prior they had been robbed."
He was not originally an ordinary person. Those who do not know him take him to be a Western Mù who merely excelled at emulating Xià Huì of Liǔxià;
they fail to realize that this old man’s hand could both kill and bring life to others. In later generations, people will have only this "donkey" remaining and no longer see such a gentleman.
This will ultimately cause the seeds of the Radiant One (*prabhāsvara*) to be severed entirely. My mind is like a mass of ink—this is truly lamentable.
Lian: Chan Master Lizong of Zihu Rock in Quzhou succeeded to the Dharma of Master Shenguang of Taizhou.
A student asked the Master, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Lychees of Fuzhou; *stathina* trees of Quanzhou.
The student asked, "What are the two characters for 'Buddha-dharma' (*buddhadharma*)? The Master said, "Just say it! The monk said, "Please, Master, say it yourself."
The Master said, "The pierced-eared barbarian monk smiles and nods his head; Master Longhua Zhao has arrived. The Master seized him and asked, "What about it?
Zhao said, "Do not mistake me. The Master then let go of him. Zhao said, "I have long admired your supreme radiance. The Master remained silent. Zhao then took his leave.
As the Master saw him off at the gate, he said, "After this parting, where shall we meet again? Zhao laughed heartily and departed.
Master Fushí of Zhāngzhōu ascended the hall and said:
"I, this mountain monk, have opened a divination shop; it can determine people's poverty or wealth and settle their life or death."
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "Setting aside birth and death, poverty and wealth, and not falling into the five elements—please, Master, speak directly.
The Master replied, "Gold, wood, water, fire, and earth."
A monk asked Master Zitong, "What is the realm of Zitong? The Master said, "Can you put sand into your own eyes?
The monk said, "I do not even recognize this 'wonderful realm of Zitong'. The Master said, "I do not conceal this matter from you. That monk—
[The monk] went out. The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Today there is a fine public case (koan).
I have not yet managed to get a single word of it into my hands. The monk said, "Fortunately, I am a monk. The Master said, "Calamity does not come alone."
When the monk Xinghua came to visit Master Rirong, the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway; who is there to oppose it?
Xinghua replied, "A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? The Master said, "Each is difficult to overcome. The Master then said, "For now..."
The public case of Xiu Weiduan was not yet resolved. The Master took his staff and danced back to the abbot’s quarters; Huo was speechless.
The Master said, "This fellow is dead!
Baotan remarked, "The former masters said that Zihu received people with a secondary capacity; this is truly the words of one who knows the authentic essence."
Nevertheless, even those four individuals, beginning with Shenguang, were all the "claws and fangs" from within the ancestral lineage.

They were like the great merchants and wealthy traders who emerge from a major capital city; whether advancing or retreating, appearing or disappearing, each possessed a portion of the single body of Master Zihu.
Had Master Zihu been a lion of the foremost capacity, the entire world would have been... [unable to contain him].
He sought out the four disciples; how much more so for Zihu?
Master Tianlong succeeded to the Dharma of National Teacher Juzhi of Mount Jinhua in Wuzhou.
When the Master first resided in a hermitage, the nun Zhiji arrived at the hut. Wearing a bamboo hat and holding a monk’s staff, she circumambulated the Master three times and said, "Speak!
The Master took off his hat; she asked this three times, but the Master gave no reply. The nun then departed.
The Master said, "It is already somewhat late; stay for one night. The nun replied, "If you can speak, then I shall stay. Again, the Master had no reply. After the nun left, the Master sighed.
He said, "Although I possess the physical form of a man, I lack the spirit of a man. I intend to abandon this hermitage and travel to various regions to seek instruction.
That night, a mountain deity informed him, "There is no need to leave this mountain. A Mahayana Bodhisattva will soon arrive to preach the Dharma for you as your preceptor.
Indeed, within ten days, Master Tianlong arrived at the hermitage. The Master then went out to welcome him and paid his respects.
He recounted the previous events. The Heavenly Dragon raised one finger to show him, and the Master attained great enlightenment on the spot.
From then on, whenever a student arrived, the Master would simply raise one finger and offer no other teaching.
Once, outside the hermitage, a boy was asked by someone, "What essential Dharma does the Master teach? The boy also raised one finger. Upon returning, he told his teacher this. The teacher—
He cut off the boy’s finger with a knife. The boy cried out and ran away. The Master called out, “Boy! whereupon the boy turned his head back. The Master held up a single finger to him;
the boy attained sudden and complete realization. As the Master was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, “I obtained the Zen of a single finger from Tianlong;
I have used it throughout my entire life and it is not yet exhausted. Having spoken these words, he departed.

Baotan said: "The single finger of Jūti possessed a strength of ten thousand *qun*. When it first brought the female bhikṣu to her knees in defeat, it was already capable of shaking the spirits of the mountains.
This shows that the power of this finger, even before its full exertion, was already such as this.
Upon seeing that Tianlong had attained realization, this finger emitted light without changing even a hair’s breadth. (The boy...)
The sword serves as the verification; this is simply what is natural for the power already unleashed by this finger.
When he was about to pass away, he said, "I have obtained the 'finger-pointing Zen' of Tianlong; I shall never exhaust its use throughout my life.
This was to direct the full force of this finger toward others. Yet, in the end, where is that which Juzhi could never exhaust? It remains right here and now.
Formerly, Chan Master Chang of Guannandao succeeded the Dharma of Venerable Dowu of Guannandao in Xiangzhou.

While traveling through a forested area, he heard a shamanist musician playing for a deity who said, "The conscious spirit is non-existent. Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly attained awakening. Later...
Chan Master Shanchang certified his understanding. He further studied under Deshan, where his realization of the Dharma flavor became even more profound.

Whenever he encountered the Master ascending the hall to instruct the assembly, he would invariably wear a lotus-patterned straw hat, don a monastic robe, and hold a ritual tablet, while beating drums and blowing flutes, addressing himself as "Third Master Lu.
At times he would say: "I beat the drum of Guannan and sing the song of Deshan. A monk asked: "What is the Patriarch?"

Regarding the Master’s intent in coming from the West, the Master greeted him with a simple bow and said, "Yes. On another occasion, the Master took a wooden sword, slung it across his shoulder, and performed a dance.
A monk asked, "Where did you get that sword in your hand? The Master threw the sword to the ground; the monk then picked it up and placed it back in the Master's hand.
The Master asked, "Where did you get it? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "I grant you three days."
The Master took up a single phrase from below; the monk had no reply. The Master himself took a sword, placed it upon his shoulder, and performed a dance, saying, "Only by doing so can one succeed.
He asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master descended from his meditation seat and performed a woman’s bow, saying, "Thank you for coming from afar;
there is nothing at all to attend to you. The Master asked Ganki, "How about you? Ganki said, "No rank. The Master—
The Master asked, "Is it not the same as empty space? Guankui said, "This butcher! The Master said, "If there were birth to be killed, one would never grow weary.
Among his fellow disciples was the Monk Luohan of Lizhou, who attained great enlightenment upon seeing Master Chang with a single punch.

Baotan said: "This was the elder brother of Linji who grew old within the Linji tradition. He refers to Linji.

Yet there are still those of the dragon species. O Lion King, I know that with a single roar, the heads of the hundred beasts would split asunder;
yet there are still lion cubs who, upon hearing this account of increased valor and strength, are filled with courage. Does this old man’s countenance perhaps surpass that of the dragon and the lion?
One can imagine that at one time, the atmosphere at the gate of Muzhou was chillingly stern. [He] sold shoes.
To feed one’s mother is this gate. To break Yunmen’s leg is this gate.
When the questioner was in the room of the Venerable Master Chen, [Muzhou] took off his sandals and struck him right over the head—this too is this gate.
Throughout their entire lives, those who have rushed about at his gate have not been one person who personally saw Muzhou, much less those born after Muzhou’s time.
The Dharma discourses cannot be recorded in full; they were all means by which Yunmen refined and forged people, much like Chen Cao and his ilk.
As for those who are like stagnant water coiled up, one must strictly avoid letting them swallow or spit out [the teachings].
When the Great Enlightenment Chan Master of Weifeng saw that Huangbo had attained deep realization, he appointed Xinghua Cunjian as the head of the monastery. The Master approached him and asked,

Xinghua shouted again. The Master struck him again. The following day, as Xinghua was passing by the Dharma Hall, the Master called out to him, "Warden!"
"I have a direct doubt regarding the shout you let out yesterday as you were walking; explain it to me.
Xinghua said, "All that Cunjiang has learned from Sansheng throughout his life has been completely overturned by you, Master.
I pray you grant me, Cunjiang, a Dharma-gate of peace and ease. The Master said, "This blind donkey, take off your patched robe; I shall give you a thorough beating. Xinghua...
Having been transformed by his words, he grasped the essential meaning; although he was a successor of Linji, he always regarded the Master as a friend who inspired and stimulated him.
When the Master was approaching death, he said to the assembly, "I have an arrow that I wish to entrust to those of this age.
A monk came forward and said, "I pray the Master will give me his arrow. The Master asked, "What do you call 'an arrow'? The monk then gave a shout. The Master struck him several times.
[The Master] went down to his own quarters. He then called the monk back in and asked, "Did you understand just now? The monk replied, "I did not understand.
The Master struck him several more times, threw down his staff, and said, "In the future, when you meet someone with clear eyes, explain this to them clearly."
Baotan said: "Linji’s one shout is like the venom of the *aconitum* (wu hui jin):
it can kill a person, yet it can also bring them back to life. It depends entirely on how it is employed. One who has not personally died at its hand and been revived is not fit to speak of this.
Why? Because for those with intellectual knowledge, this shout is medicine; for those who are mere students, it is a disease. When...
In the lineage of Huangbo, everyone employs this medicine. In later generations, there are those who act as skilled physicians by examining the complexion and listening to the voice.

As for Dajue’s treatment of Xinghua, a single dose of *wuwei* (aconite) cured his chronic, terminal ailment. Those worldly scholars and mediocre physicians, however, do not understand the past or the present;
even if their lungs and livers were sliced open and shown to them, they would still be unable to discern it. This is truly lamentable.
How tragic! Those who study Chan should investigate the essential tenets of Huangbo; those who study medicine should master the diagnostic insights of Lu and Bian.
Beyond this, what else remains to be said?

[The monk] said, "I see. The Master asked, "What artifice are you using? He replied, "I see that I cannot employ even a single artifice.
The Master struck him. Hu Dingjiao came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao? He replied, "I dare not say so.
The Master said, "Can you still nail the void? He replied, "Please have the Master break it open; I will nail it for you. The Master—
He struck him with his staff. The monk said, "Preceptor, do not strike me in error. The Master said, "In the future, there will be many talkative masters who will explain this for you.
A monk asked, "What is it like when there is not a single cloud ten thousand miles away? The Master said, "Even the blue sky must eat a blow of the staff."
Chan Master Huiran of Sansheng Monastery in Zhenzhou had received the essential instructions from Linji. Upon arriving at Yangshan, Yangshan asked him, "What is your name? The Master replied:
His name was Huìjì. Yangshan said, "Huìjì is my name. The Master said, "My name is Huìrán. Yangshan simply laughed loudly.
When the Master arrived at Xiangyan, Xiangyan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Linji. Xiangyan said, "Have you brought Linji’s sword with you?
The Master suddenly struck him over the mouth with his sitting cloth and departed. When the Master arrived at Deshan... [he just] entered.
He spread out his sitting mat. Deshan said, "Do not spread out your napkin; there is no rice here. The Master said, "Even if there were, there would be nowhere to put it.
Deshan struck him with his staff. The Master caught it and instead pushed Deshan onto the meditation seat.
Deshan laughed loudly. The Master went away, crying out to the blue heavens. While the Master was at Xuefeng, he heard Feng deliver this statement:
"Every person possesses a face that is an ancient mirror. This monkey also possesses a face that is an ancient mirror.
The Master came out and asked, "It has been nameless throughout kalpas; why does the Abbot establish it as an 'ancient mirror'? Feng said, "A flaw has arisen.
The Master scolded him, saying, "You old monk do not even recognize the point of this discourse! Feng said, "I am at fault. The Elder Monk has many administrative duties."
When the Master saw Baoshou open the hall for teaching, he pushed a monk forward to stand before Baoshou. Baoshou then struck that monk.
The Master said, "Elder, if you act as a teacher in this manner, you will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou."

Baotán said: "In the lineage of Linjì, there were Bǎoshòu, Sāngshèng, and Xìnghuà, just as in the lineage of Mázǔ, there were Bǎizhàng, Nánquán, and Guīzōng. Bǎizhàng resembled Mázǔ yet possessed great vigor;
Guīzōng resembled Mázǔ yet was utterly bold and spirited; Nánquán resembled Mázǔ yet was utterly expansive. From this we know..."
Baoshou resembles Linji in his earnestness and substance; Sansheng resembles Linji in his vigor and brilliance; Xinghua resembles Linji in his profound purity.
This earnestness and substance is seen in the place where he was struck with a staff while under the blue sky, and in the place where he struck the iron riveter.
Jung-fa was seen at the place where Zhaozhou struck Xiangyan;
Yuan-cui was seen at the place where he overturned Deshan and extinguished the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.
Although each attained one aspect, they still rank as Linji masters for a hundred generations—how much more so for those who have attained the whole! How could it be otherwise?

Was it not for the sake of ten million generations that Linji appeared? I have often lamented that the staff and shout were not employed in this present age, and thus the Way of Linji has become obscure.
Is it because the strength of later students is insufficient to sustain it, or is it because their teachers have failed to fully exhaust its essential meaning?
As the saying goes, "When a person drinks water, they know its coldness or warmth themselves. One tael of incense from Xinghua...
Incense. It was obtained through great hardship and toil, which is why it is so magnificent.
Once, when Chan Master Xinghua Cunjian of Weifeng asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
the monk replied, "From the place of Master Cuiyan. The Master said, "Did you bring back Master Cuiyan’s shout?"
"Have you come? he asked. The monk replied, "I have not come with anything. The Master said, "In that case, you have not come from the place of Cui Chan.
The monk shouted. The Master struck him. The Master said to the assembly, "I hear shouting in the long corridors and shouting in the back quarters.
My sons, do not shout blindly or recklessly. Even if you could shout so skillfully as to make Xinghua dwell in the midst of the heavens, [you would still] fall down."
His breath was nearly spent. Waiting for Xinghua to recover and rise, he said to him, "I have not yet finished. Why is this?
I have never scattered real pearls from within a purple silk curtain for you all; why do you shout wildly in empty space?
If I were to stretch my hand across your face twice, you would be unable to leave. One day—
He said to the rector, Kebin: "Before long, you shall become a master of the liturgical chant. Kebin replied, "I will not enter this monastic community.
The Master asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you have understood, or because you have not? Kebin said, "It is neither of these. The Master struck him and addressed the assembly:
"The rector Kebin has been defeated in the battle of Dharma; he must forfeit five strings of cash for his robes and bowl."
He punished them by having them eat a meal together in one hall and then drove them out of the monastery. A monk asked, "What was the meaning of the National Teacher calling for the attendant?

The Master said, "One blind man leading a crowd of blind men. On another occasion, the Master called out to a monk, "So-and-so! The monk responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Pointing at it, he does not reach it.
Then he called another monk; the monk responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Reaching it, he does not point at it. [This concludes the record of] Tang Zhuangzong.
The Emperor said to the Master, "When I captured the Great Liang, I obtained a priceless pearl, yet no one has come forward to appraise its value.
The Master replied, "I beg Your Majesty to let me see the pearl. The Emperor extended the flap of his *fuhetou* (a head-wrap) for him to view.
The Master said, "Who would dare to appraise the treasure of a sovereign? Thereupon, he became the teacher of Emperor Tongguang.
Baotán said: "Línjì’s single shout is like the pearl from beneath the chin of a black dragon; only those who dare to provoke its逆鱗 (nǐlín—'scales on the nape') can obtain it.
This pearl is called the *vaśī-ratna* (wish-fulfilling gem), which appears blue when seen as blue, and yellow when seen as yellow.
Sāngshèng and Dàjué were those who provoked the scales and obtained the pearl; Xìnghuà died later."
On the day of opening the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "This single incense offering would properly belong to my elder brother, Master Sansheng.
But Master Sansheng is too distant for me. I wish to offer it to my elder brother, Master Dajue, yet Master Dajue is too solitary for me.
It is better, therefore, to make offerings to our late master Linji. Otherwise, how could I give rise to the true lineage of our Linji?"

The lineage of the patriarchal heirs: the Dharma is fundamentally without flaw; it is people themselves who perceive it as flawed. When one hears Linji’s shout, even those present are struck dumb—how could there be any flaw in that?
Examining Xinghua’s words, one can imagine that at that time there were also those who manipulated the texts and played fast and loose with the Law.
Xinghua said: "I hear shouting in the eastern corridor and shouting in the western corridor. I am waiting for you..."
He drank until Xinghua was sent soaring toward the heavens; when he fell down, there was not a breath of life left in him.
Slowly rising, he said to you: "It is not yet finished. Why? Because I have never, before this, scattered genuine pearls from within a purple silk curtain for you all.
Furthermore, the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says: "For example, suppose there were a person who falsely claimed to be an emperor..."
To seize and execute [the Buddha]—how much more so for the Dharma King! What kind of thought would such a person harbor?
Regarding "Examining the Fellow Practitioner," it says: "I held my hand across his face twice, and he could not leave.
Now, where was it that he held his hand across his face twice? Those with eyes to see should look.
When Master Zhufu, whose secular name was Zhiyi, first questioned Linji, he asked:
"What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'? Linji replied: "The spring sun brings forth life, spreading carpets of brocade;
the infant’s white hair hangs down like silk. The Master then asked: "What is 'taking away the environment but not..."
"Seizing both man and object. Linji said, "The King’s command has been issued and has spread throughout the world; the General has cleared the frontier beyond the borders, leaving no smoke or dust.
The Master asked, "What is it like when neither man nor object is seized? Linji said, "The King ascends the precious throne; the village elder sings his song."
The Master asked, "What is meant by 'the person and the environment are both taken away'? Linji replied, "In Bing and Fen, speech is cut off; dwelling alone in one place.

At these words, the Master realized the essential meaning and entered deeply into the Dharma-gates of the Three Mysteries, the Three Essentials, and the Four Propositions, which greatly assisted his path of transformation.
Baotán said: Some may say that Nanyue and Mazu did not possess this Dharma.

If so, from what source did this Dharma arise differently when the two elders, Linji and Huangbo, flourished and expanded their Way? During the time of Nanyue and Mazu, the faculties [of beings] were as superior as those in spring;
they were imbued with such great harmony that no trace of artifice or display was seen. By the time of Linji’s era, the faculties [of beings] were like...

It is summer and autumn; as the days pass, the vigorous energy wanes. Only after the stern and killing [energies] do they achieve their fulfillment. Thus, the roots correspond to the four seasons, and the Dharma is likewise like the four seasons.
A good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) grasps the power of creation and transformation, yet the traces of this shifting and turning are not seen.
Linji’s Four Kinds of Critical Examination were devised because he deeply foresaw that future generations would fail to understand his essential teaching and would instead fall into error.
Regarding the "Deviant Paths," he expounded upon it by means of a four-line verse to bring it into clear light.
If students can, like Ke Fu, penetrate deeply into the gates of the Three Mysteries, the Three Essentials, and the Four Lines, only then will they know that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary sentiment.
